items.text: Norma J. Torres is the U.S. Representative for California's 35th District and has served in Congress since 2015. She was a 9-1-1 dispatcher before beginning her political career on the Pomona City Council and as the city's mayor. She later served in the California State Assembly and State Senate. In Congress she sits on the Appropriations Committee.

sentences.text: Norma J. Torres is the U.S. Representative for California's 35th District and has served in Congress since 2015.
She was a 9-1-1 dispatcher before beginning her political career on the Pomona City Council and as the city's mayor.
She later served in the California State Assembly and State Senate.
In Congress she sits on the Appropriations Committee.

items.text: In 2026 she introduced the Better Pay for American Workers Act and the National Parent and Youth Helpline Act. She also introduced the Violent Insurrection Recidivist Enhancement Act of 2026. She has proposed the Multiple Firearm Sales Reporting Modernization Act, which requires reporting sales of long guns within five days, and the 911 SAVES Act to reclassify 9-1-1 professionals as first responders. Her campaign notes she voted to pass the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which allocated funds for Ontario International Airport. She also supported the CHIPS and Science Act and the Inflation Reduction Act. Her campaign says her Central American Women and Children Act was implemented as the first compact between the U.S. and Honduras to address gender-based violence. It also states she passed the Enrique Roman-Martinez Military Cold Case Justice Act to reform how the military handles cold cases. Her campaign says that in 2022 she secured $40.7 million for water recycling in Ontario, $16 million for stormwater infrastructure in Fontana, and $27.5 million for wastewater projects in Rialto.
